title: Ice crystal habit
help: Classify the 3D crystal you think it is, not the 2D outline: a plate seen edge-on looks like a thin column, a short column seen end-on looks like a hexagon. For aggregates, fragments and graupel, also say what it is made of, if you can tell. Hollow and Chain appear beside the classes they apply to; Rimed works on any class. If you're not sure, give your best guess with Unsure, or use Can't tell rather than guessing.

classes.name: Droplet
classes.desc: Liquid drop: a near-perfect circle with a smooth edge, usually with a bright spot or ring in the middle where it focuses the light.

classes.name: Quasi-sphere
classes.desc: Round but not quite a perfect circle, no bright centre: frozen drop or small quasi-spherical ice.

classes.name: Column
classes.desc: Hexagonal prism longer than wide, flat ends; a short column seen end-on looks like a hexagon. Length about equal to width: call it a column if the ends look flat and sharp, a plate if it looks thin. Hollow? Tick Hollow (H).

classes.name: Needle
classes.desc: Very long thin column (aspect ratio above about 5).

classes.name: Plate
classes.desc: Thin hexagonal plate or sectored plate, including tilted and edge-on plates (thin, straight-sided). Thicker than wide? That's a column. Hollowed (skeletal)? Tick Hollow (H).

classes.name: Bullet rosette
classes.desc: Several columns or bullets radiating from one centre.

classes.name: Side planes / polycrystal
classes.desc: Crystal with plates growing out of it at different angles (side planes), or an irregular polycrystal made of several crystals grown together rather than stuck together. Common at about −20 to −40 °C.

classes.name: Bullet
classes.desc: A single bullet: one arm broken off a bullet rosette (a column with one pointed end).

classes.name: Capped column
classes.desc: Column with plates on one or both ends. Rimed? Add the Rimed flag (R).

classes.name: Scroll / sheath
classes.desc: Thin sheet of ice curled into a hollow, open-sided column (scroll), or a long hollow sheath.

classes.name: Aggregate
classes.desc: Several crystals stuck together. Say what of, if you can tell, and tick Chain (N) if they're linked end to end.

classes.name: Fragment
classes.desc: A broken piece of a larger crystal. Say what of, if you can tell.

classes.name: Graupel
classes.desc: So heavily rimed that the original crystal can't be made out: lumpy, rounded outline. If you can still tell the habit, use that class with the Rimed flag (R) instead. Say what it was, if you can tell.

classes.name: Irregular
classes.desc: Ice with no recognisable habit, and not side planes or a polycrystal.

classes.name: Too small to tell
classes.desc: Fewer than about 15 pixels across (roughly 35 µm on a CPI): too few pixels to judge the habit.

classes.name: Can't tell / blurred
classes.desc: Out of focus, overlapping, or otherwise unclassifiable.

classes.name: Artefact
classes.desc: Not a cloud particle: shattering debris, streaks, smudges, stuck particle, empty ROI.

flags.name: Rimed
flags.desc: Some riming visible, but you can still tell what the crystal is (e.g. a rimed capped column). If riming hides the shape, use Graupel.

flags.name: Hollow
flags.desc: Hollow column, or hollowed (skeletal) plate: a bright, empty-looking interior.

flags.name: Chain
flags.desc: Crystals linked end to end in a chain, rather than a clump.

flags.name: Cut off
flags.desc: Particle runs off the edge of the image.

flags.name: Unsure
flags.desc: Your best guess, but you're not confident.
